description: Agent GovCon: submit an invoice or payment voucher with the contract’s payment terms and the acceptance record it bills: the invoice with its number, the contract number it bills, the currency, each line with its id, line item number, the deliverable or work it bills, the first and last day it bills for, quantity, unit price and amount, and the total; the contract with its number, currency, each line item number the award carries, the last day the obligated funding covers and the last day of the period of performance; the acceptance records with each line item or deliverable accepted, the day and the value accepted. The signed report gives the invoice and the contract, each line item read against the award, each line and the total recomputed, each line read against the acceptance record for what it bills, and each billed period read against the earlier of the funded period and the period of performance, and counts them, and names a divergent invoice: an amount unlike the accepted deliverable it bills or in another currency, a charge against a contract line item the award does not carry, a total that does not recompute, and billing for a period past the funding or performance period the award states; then a line with no acceptance record and another contract number, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No lines, no line items on the award, no total or line arithmetic, no acceptance records, or no funded period or end of performance leaves those points unverified. Line items compare by their letters and digits, amounts to the cent in one currency, deliverables by their words, and periods by the day. This reads the invoice against the contract and the acceptance record as stated. Verdict govcon_invoice_divergent, govcon_invoice_partial, govcon_invoice_unverified or govcon_invoice_consistent. POST /api/govcon-invoice-check. Reads the government contracting records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between contracting documents only: it never submits a bid or proposal, never registers or certifies a vendor in any government system, never contacts an agency and never decides eligibility or award, which stay with the contracting agency, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent GovCon reads government contracting records across the procurement lifecycle for consistency between the documents and the terms they answer to: a solicitation, a vendor’s eligibility record, a proposal or bid, a price proposal or pricing volume, an award notice, a contract modification, a deliverable or progress report and an invoice or payment voucher, each against its own sections and the notice it follows, the solicitation’s set-aside, eligibility, submission and pricing terms, the winning price and eligibility record, the base award and prior modifications, the deliverable schedule, or the payment terms and acceptance record it should agree with. The family reads procurement, the government buying goods and services under contract terms, and reads the records against each other. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-govcon-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-govcon/.
